The governing v2 script was a FULL REWRITE executed under the teaser-v2 standard the same day: its change log items 1–2 record both strips, its N-09 audit passes on the fresh wording, and this migration verified by direct reading that neither device appears in v2's nine lines. All three records stand as written; the package carries the FAIL as the board carries it and the strips as the doc records them, and takes no side on the board's bookkeeping.

THE GOVERNING DOC'S '118 SPOKEN WORDS' DOES NOT REPRODUCE AS A SPOKEN COUNT. v2 §4 heads its script '134 tokens counted mechanically… 118 spoken words + 16 bridge words'. Counted at this migration from the §4 text (whitespace split; a standalone em dash is a mechanical token, not a spoken word; the bracketed bridge label excluded as a stage direction): mechanical 20/21/15/19/7/14/12/10/16 = 134 (the printed mechanical total is EXACT); standalone dashes 4 (L1 ×2, L4 ×2); spoken 18/21/15/17/7/14/12/10/16 = 130 in total. The printed 118 equals the MECHANICAL count of lines 1–8 — dashes included — wearing the spoken label; the spoken count of lines 1–8 is 114. The bridge figure (16) is exact under both rulers. The doc's runtime projection ('118 spoken words × 0.45 s/word ≈ 53 s speech; ≈57–58 s total') inherits the 118: on the spoken count the same arithmetic gives ≈51 s of speech. The projection stands as the doc's own, carried not corrected; both rulers for both versions are printed in transcript/transcript.md. The same looseness appears once in prose: DR-2 calls L5 'five words of verdict' — L5 counts 7 tokens under either ruler.
